entries.title: II Samuel 1:2
segments: Many will pay court to those who are to have power, hoping in this way to obtain their favor and gain promotion.

entries.title: II Samuel 1:10
segments: The courses wicked men take for their own advancement, often prove the occasion of their ruin.

entries.title: II Samuel 1:11
segments: Rent them; in token of anguish.

entries.title: II Samuel 1:12
segments: A good man will not desire the death even of his bitterest enemy, though it would open the way to his own elevation, influence, and honor.

entries.title: II Samuel 1:14
segments: The Lord's anointed; him whom God had anointed to be king.

entries.title: II Samuel 1:17
segments: It is proper to lament the death of those with whom we have been connected; and while we bow with submission to the afflicting hand of God, we should acknowledge with gratitude his goodness in the natural endowments as well as the spiritual blessings which he bestowed on them.

entries.title: II Samuel 1:18
segments:
The bow; some suppose this to be the title of the poem which follows.  2Sa 1.29-27 
 
  The book of Jasher;

entries.title: II Samuel 1:19
segments: The beauty of Israel is slain upon thy high places; that is, Saul and Jonathan, here called the beauty or glory of Israel.

entries.title: II Samuel 1:21
segments: As though he had not been anointed with oil; he has perished in dishonor, as though he had been a common man, and not the Lord's anointed.

entries.title: II Samuel 1:23
segments: Lovely and pleasant; that is, in their relation to each other. Though Jonathan was the firm friend of David, yet he remained faithful to his father; and Saul, except in some moments of jealousy, honored Jonathan with his entire confidence.

It is worthy of remark how David mentions what was good in Saul, omitting his faults. 
 
vv 23-24 In speaking of the dead it is proper to omit all notice of their faults, except when the cause of truth requires that they be mentioned.

entries.title: II Samuel 1:24
segments: Clothed you in scarlet--put on ornaments of gold; the reference is probably to the spoil taken from the enemies of Israel, with which he enriched the Israelitish women.

entries.title: II Samuel 1:26
segments: The most intimate and endearing friendships must soon be broken; but if founded in true piety, they will be revived again never to be interrupted, but to become more and more intimate and endearing for ever.
